meta.description: Tests a gene list (ORA, enrichWP) or a ranked gene vector (GSEA, gseWP) against the WikiPathways community-curated pathway collection with clusterProfiler and rWikiPathways. Covers why a WikiPathways result is a snapshot of a live, monthly-updated database (enrichWP/gseWP/gson_WP silently pull data.wikipathways.org/current/), why reproducibility requires pinning a dated GMT via downloadPathwayArchive(date=, format='gmt'), why the WP GMT is Entrez-keyed so symbols and Ensembl silently overlap nothing, why universe=NULL gives a biased all-WP-genes background, how to split the name%version%wpid%org term, and why WikiPathways (CC0, no peer review) complements KEGG/Reactome.
meta.executed_inputs: 7/7 (input 4's SKILL.md/usage-guide.md example date 404s against the live server -- executed anyway with a currently-valid date to test the mechanism itself; the shipped examples/wikipathways_explore.R was also run byte-for-byte and halts at the identical call; see P1)

scientific_integrity.detail: All executed numbers come from live runs against the real WikiPathways API/GMT archive and real org.Hs.eg.db annotations (clusterProfiler 4.14.6, rWikiPathways 1.26.0, org.Hs.eg.db 3.20.0). DE hit/background labels and the log2FC/padj values are synthetic and labeled as such in data/make_wp_inputs.R; the six cited references (Pico 2008 PLoS Biol, Martens 2021 NAR, Agrawal 2024 NAR, Hanspers 2020 Genome Biol, Shin 2023 BMC Genomics, Wu 2021 Innovation) are real, correctly attributed WikiPathways/clusterProfiler papers.

practice_boundaries.detail: Gene-set/pathway enrichment on de-identified expression data only; no individual-level, diagnostic, or prescriptive content; no disclaimer required for this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill's central methodological claim (unpinned universe=NULL biases the background and inflates significance) was independently reproduced and is the correct statistical framing; the ORA/GSEA method split, BH adjustment, and community-vs-peer-reviewed-source caveats are all sound. No fallacy found in any of the seven executed patterns.

code_usability.detail: All seven R patterns ran to completion (enrichWP, gseWP with seeded determinism, universe comparison, enricher on a dated GMT, compareCluster, cross-species enrichWP, and the documented SYMBOL-not-converted failure mode). The shipped examples/wikipathways_ora.R ran end-to-end verbatim, unmodified, and produced correct output. examples/wikipathways_explore.R halts with an unhandled R error ('Execution halted') when run top-to-bottom, unmodified, at the exact same downloadPathwayArchive(date='20240310', ...) call -- confirmed by running the shipped file byte-for-byte, not just the SKILL.md prose example. The call itself, its arguments, and the downstream read.gmt()/separate()/enricher() logic are all correct (verified end-to-end once a currently-valid date was substituted); the defect is a stale hardcoded date literal against a live server with a 12-month retention window, not a syntax error, missing dependency, or logic bug, so this stays PASS rather than triggering M4 -- but it is scored down under Functional Suitability/Maintainability and is the audit's top P1 (see below).

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4/4 (ORA, GSEA, dated-GMT reproducibility, direct DB queries, multi-organism, WP-vs-KEGG/Reactome contrast, PFOCR scoping, all covered). Appropriateness 4/4 (clusterProfiler+rWikiPathways is exactly the right stack; scope cleanly deferred to sibling Skills). Correctness 3/4: every mechanistic claim this audit checked held (universe=NULL inflation, Entrez-only GMT, searchPathways removal, format=gpml default, BridgeDb xref codes, get_wp_organisms), but the one worked reproducibility example (date='20240310') is stale -- it 404s today because the live archive retains only 12 months, and the Skill never states that retention window (P1).

reliability.note: Category-3 override applied: Mode A instructional skill, so documented failure-mode tables substitute for in-code error handling. Error Reporting 4/4 (an 8-row Common Errors table plus a parallel Per-Method Failure Modes section, both symptom->cause->fix, both spot-checked and accurate). Fault Tolerance 3/4 and Recoverability 3/4: thorough for ID-type/universe/date-format pitfalls but silent on the archive-retention 404 and the wrong-organism-string silent-NULL case, both reproduced live this pass (P1, P2).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 207 lines with depth correctly pushed to usage-guide.md and examples/; workflow is linear (bitr -> enrichWP/gseWP -> setReadable -> read result) with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4, Consistency 4, Feedback Design 4 (documented output columns exactly matched what enrichWP/gseWP/compareCluster returned in every run). Error Prevention 3/4: proactively warns against the ID-type, universe, current/-drift, and gpml-default pitfalls, but not the archive-retention-window trap that this audit's own SKILL.md-documented example hit.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 3/4 (precise but dense, technical trigger language typical of this Skill family). Category-3 override applied to Forgiveness: 3/4 -- the underlying functions degrade to a clean NULL/empty result rather than a crash or a silently-wrong number on bad ID types or organism strings, which is the correct data-integrity posture, not a usability defect.

inputs.label: universe=NULL vs a matched tested-gene universe, on both a null gene list and the planted-signal list
inputs.note: Direct, live reproduction of the SKILL's central safety claim. On the planted-signal list, background N jumped from 186 (matched universe, tested-genes-annotated-in-WP) to 9031 (default universe=NULL, all-WP-genes) for the identical WP554 hit, and its p.adjust dropped from 6.86e-11 to 9.34e-39 -- roughly 28 orders of magnitude more 'significant' purely from the biased background, exactly the direction and mechanism the SKILL.md Common Errors table describes. On a 150-gene list with NO planted biology, neither universe setting fabricated a false hit (0 terms both ways -- too few of the 150 random genes clear the WP minGSSize=10 annotation floor to test the inflation effect on a true null; a minor gap in this input's design, not a Skill defect).

inputs.label: Reproducible analysis: pin a dated GMT, split the term field, run enricher on the pinned sets, report the date
inputs.note: The exact worked example in both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md, downloadPathwayArchive(date='20240310', organism='Homo sapiens', format='gmt'), returns an HTTP 404 today (2026-09-17): data.wikipathways.org's own index page states it retains only 'the last 12 months' of monthly archives, and the live folder listing confirms it -- entries jump from a 3-file 20230810 stray straight to 20260110, i.e. every monthly folder between Aug 2023 and Jan 2026 is gone. Substituting a currently-valid date (20260810) made the rest of the documented pattern work exactly as described: read.gmt() -> separate(term, c('name','version','wpid','org'), sep='%') -> enricher(TERM2GENE=, TERM2NAME=) recovered both planted terms (WP554 p.adjust 6.4e-11, WP430 p.adjust 8.9e-22) from a term list that split cleanly into all four documented fields. gson_WP() also ran without error, consistent with the SKILL's claim that it snapshots current/ rather than pinning a date.

key_strengths: The Skill's central safety claim -- an unpinned universe=NULL biases the background and inflates significance -- was reproduced almost exactly as described: the same true-positive term's p.adjust dropped from 6.9e-11 to 9.3e-39 (about 28 orders of magnitude) purely from swapping the background from the tested-gene universe to the default.

All seven executed R patterns (ORA, seeded/deterministic GSEA, universe comparison, dated-GMT reproducibility mechanics, compareCluster up/down, cross-species zebrafish enrichment, and the documented SYMBOL-into-Entrez-GMT failure mode) ran against live WikiPathways data and recovered real, planted pathway signal with correct statistics.

Every one of the SKILL's documented API/failure-mode claims this audit spot-checked (searchPathways() removal, format defaulting to gpml, get_wp_organisms(), the three BridgeDb xref codes, the silent-empty-result on non-Entrez IDs) reproduced exactly as claimed on the installed clusterProfiler 4.14.6 / rWikiPathways 1.26.0.

Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples/ layering with a precise, specific trigger description and explicit scope handoffs to five sibling Skills, all consistent with what this Skill actually produces.

recommendations.title: Reproducibility worked example uses a date the live archive no longer serves
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's and usage-guide.md's own 'correct, reproducible pattern' example, downloadPathwayArchive(date='20240310', organism='Homo sapiens', format='gmt'), returns an HTTP 404 today because data.wikipathways.org retains only the last 12 months of monthly archives; nothing in the Skill states this retention window or names the Zenodo GMT/GPML archive that WikiPathways' own site recommends for anything older. This is not just a documentation staleness issue: the shipped examples/wikipathways_explore.R file itself, run byte-for-byte unmodified, halts on this exact call ('Execution halted').
recommendations.root_cause: The reproducibility guidance treats the dated-archive endpoint as a permanent pin when it is only durable for about a year on WikiPathways' own infrastructure.
recommendations.fix: Replace the hardcoded date in both worked examples with guidance to use a date within the last 12 months, and add one sentence noting the retention window plus the Zenodo GMT/GPML community archive (https://zenodo.org/communities/wikipathways) as the citable long-term fallback for anything published beyond that window.

recommendations.title: Wrong-organism-string failure mode is undocumented
recommendations.problem: enrichWP(organism='zebrafish') (a plausible common-name mistake instead of the required scientific binomial) returns NULL silently, but this specific symptom is absent from the otherwise-thorough Common Errors and Per-Method Failure Modes tables, which only say to verify the string first without saying what a wrong one does.
recommendations.root_cause: The failure-mode tables were written around the ID-type, universe, and date/format pitfalls but not the free-text organism parameter, which fails the same silent-NULL way.
recommendations.fix: Add one row to the Common Errors table: 'enrichWP/gseWP returns NULL with no terms | wrong/non-canonical organism string | verify with listOrganisms()/get_wp_organisms() first; the string must match exactly.'
